claims_disputed.reason: The large gain appears only on D_real (Table IV: Direct F1 63.27 to DRA 96.73), and D_real was sampled 200/200 from DRA's own predictions with labels produced by correcting those predictions (8 FP / 5 FN, §V-A), so it favours DRA by construction. On D_syn, the only set not seeded from DRA output, Direct-only F1 is 95.36 vs DRA 96.16 and accuracy 95.54 vs 96.25: under 1 pp on 560 items, single run, no variance.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The AST/inter-procedural code-bundle (depth k=3, sensitive-API extraction) is used but never compared with an alternative (entry function only, whole file, no sensitive-API list). App. A only justifies k=3 by call-depth statistics, not by detection accuracy. The review's own note says 'not ablated separately'.

The paper measures description fidelity of third-party MCP tools (Table V), but never compares MCP with another integration layer and never measures agent outcomes (§V-D is 8 illustrative cases). It has no positive evidence for MCP, so 'mixed' implies a balance the paper does not show; the DCI hazard applies to any description-driven tool layer.

missed_issues: Population recall can be estimated from the paper's own numbers: 5 FN in 200 predicted-consistent pairs (2.5%) extrapolated to the ~15,123 predicted-consistent valid pairs gives ~378 missed DCIs vs ~1,831 true positives (1,907 x 192/200), i.e. recall ~83%, not 97.46%. Precision (~96%) is unaffected because the flagged stratum was sampled directly.

D_real labels were produced by validating DCIChecker's predicted labels (§V-A); the paper does not say annotators were blind to the prediction, and it reports no inter-annotator agreement (only 'disagreements resolved by a third senior researcher'). Anchoring bias is likely.

The subtype distribution (Fig. 4: Func-Over 35.4%, Func-Un 22.8%, ...) is never validated on real data; subtype accuracy is only reported on D_syn, where Func-Am coverage is 26/40 (Table III). Finding 3 rests on unvalidated LLM subtype labels.
Func-Am ('description too vague') is a subjective quality judgement counted as inconsistency, which inflates the headline 9.93% prevalence relative to strict code/description contradiction.
D_syn inconsistencies were generated by an LLM and then detected by an LLM; mutation artifacts may be easier for an LLM judge than organic drift (other:synthetic_llm_mutations).
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats. The review already flags the self-sampled D_real set. It still credits AST extraction (P05) with support that was never ablated, and accepts the DRA ablation as moderate even though the independent synthetic set shows under 1 pp of gain. Using the paper's own FN rate, population recall is about 83%.
